implementation_statement: Group POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) applies. Carrier access procedures for OSS, BSS, and network elements are kept in the Carrier supplement and platform runbooks.

Workforce and outsourced agent accounts for SYS-C1 to SYS-C4 come from SYS-G1 identity governance, driven by HR and vendor events. Gap: in the acquired regions, about 38% of access-network elements and 22 SBCs still use shared local administrator accounts outside identity governance (gap 1; POAM-010). Outsourced agent leavers are reported weekly (POAM-001).
evidence: Identity governance export; network element account inventory; vendor leaver reports

implementation_statement: Provisioning, disabling, and certification campaigns are automated in SYS-G1 identity governance for all IT applications in the boundary.

control_name: Automated Temporary and Emergency Account Management
implementation_statement: Temporary and emergency accounts expire automatically (default 30 days; break-glass accounts sealed and reviewed after use).
Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically, including outsourced agent accounts.
The SOC alerts on atypical use of BSS agent accounts (bulk CDR views, after-hours searches, VIP account lookups) and of OSS administrator accounts.
evidence: SIEM use cases for BSS and OSS

implementation_statement: Role-based access is enforced in the BSS, OSS, mediation, and portal. Gap: the shared service assurance platform's tenant partition is incomplete. A legacy role held by about 410 Engineering and 60 Tower operators can read Carrier trouble tickets that contain CPNI (gap 2; POAM-008).
evidence: Role catalog; service assurance tenant configuration; P07 test queries

implementation_statement: Flows between the OSS/BSS, the management plane, and other zones go through the provider A hub and regional NOC firewalls with deny-by-default rules. CDR extracts leave only through approved interfaces.
evidence: Hub and NOC firewall rule sets

implementation_statement: Duties are separated between BSS configuration, billing operations, and CPNI approval administration; network change approval is separate from implementation.
Least privilege is applied through role design and quarterly certification. Gap: the cross-tenant read role on the service assurance platform gives affiliate operators more than they need (POAM-008).
Security functions (AAA policy, CPNI flag administration, mediation configuration) are restricted to named administrator roles.
Privileged IT access is granted just in time through PAM with approval and session recording. Network element privileges in the legacy regions follow AC-2 above.
Privileged and CPNI-capable roles are recertified each quarter by data owners.
Privileged functions are logged to the SIEM from PAM, cloud audit logs, and AAA accounting (legacy regions excepted; see AU-12).
Workforce accounts lock after 10 failed attempts; customer portal accounts lock after 5 and require a one-time code to the number or email of record.
Endpoints lock after 10 minutes idle (group endpoint baseline).
BSS agent sessions end after 30 minutes idle; OSS and element manager sessions after 15 minutes.

Remote workforce access uses the group zero-trust access service with MFA. Gap: Engineering's SYS-E1 keeps persistent site-to-site tunnels into the management plane in the acquired regions (gap 7; POAM-024).

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote access sessions are encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher or IPsec using approved algorithms.
Remote administration of OSS/BSS components is routed through managed access points (zero-trust access service and regional jump hosts).
Use of external systems with Carrier data requires a contract with CPNI and security terms (POL-01 4.8); personal devices may reach the BSS only through managed browsers.

responsible_role: Carrier Senior Vice President, Regulatory and Compliance
implementation_statement: CPNI disclosures to agents are made under contracts. Gap: there is no intercompany CPNI agreement with the Engineering and Tower divisions, and a 2026 Engineering sales campaign used Carrier enterprise CPNI without an approval check or campaign record (gap 2; POAM-009).
Group awareness and training policy and procedures apply (POL-01).
Annual security awareness for all workforce users and outsourced agents, with phishing simulations each quarter.
Awareness includes pretexting and social engineering aimed at CPNI (callers impersonating customers, data brokers, and law enforcement).

Role-based CPNI training covers when CPNI may and may not be used, authentication, and discipline. Gap: outsourced agents are at 74% completion and affiliate operators with ticket access have never been trained (POAM-015).
Group logging standard applies: 1 year searchable in the SIEM and 6 years archived.
Logged events for the boundary are defined in the logging standard and the platform log catalog (authentication, privilege use, CPNI views, CDR exports, configuration changes).
BSS and portal logs record user, account, CPNI fields viewed, channel, and result; OSS logs record ticket and element identifiers.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews and analyzes boundary logs continuously with correlation rules. Gap: network element logs from the acquired regions are not reviewed (gap 1; POAM-003).
Review, analysis, and reporting are integrated through the SIEM and security orchestration.
Logs from the BSS, OSS, cloud, identity, and EDR are correlated across divisions in one SIEM.
Logs are written to a separate log archive account with object lock; SOC and platform administrators cannot delete them.
Logs are retained 1 year searchable and 6 years archived; the CPNI breach record is kept at least 2 years (64.2011(d)).
Components generate audit records as defined in AU-2. Gap: object-level read logging is not enabled on the CDR store, so the Carrier could not tell which CDRs an intruder read (POAM-014).
Group assessment and authorization procedures apply (POL-01 4.9).
Group internal audit assesses common controls once and samples division controls each year (P07).
Assessors are independent: internal audit reports to the board audit committee and does not operate controls.

Interconnections with SYS-C6, SYS-C7, SYS-C9, and SYS-C10 are documented. Gap: the SYS-E1 tunnels and the tenant arrangements on the service assurance platform have no interconnection or intercompany security agreement (POAM-026).
The P07 POA&M tracks every weakness with an owner and date.
Authorization equivalent: authorized to operate with conditions on 2026-09-17 by the Group CISO and the Group Chief Risk Officer (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring through SIEM, vulnerability scanning, configuration compliance, and quarterly control metrics to the Group CISO.
Risk monitoring feeds the group and Carrier registers quarterly (NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1 roll-up).
Annual external penetration test of the portal, API gateway, and cloud boundary; network element testing is included from 2027.
Group configuration management standard applies.
Baselines are kept as code for cloud components and as golden configurations for network element classes in SYS-C5.
Changes go through the Carrier change advisory board with risk rating, test evidence, and backout plans; emergency changes are reviewed within 2 business days.
Security impact analysis is required for changes to authentication, CPNI handling, and management plane access.
Only change-approved roles can deploy to production, enforced by pipeline permissions and PAM.
Guardrail policies enforce secure configuration of cloud resources; network element settings are checked nightly against golden configurations.
Unneeded services are disabled per baseline; management interfaces of network elements are bound to the management VRF.
Component inventory is kept in the OSS network inventory and the cloud asset inventory, reconciled weekly.
Inventory is updated as part of every installation, removal, and provisioning order.
Planned: a CPNI data map showing where CPNI is stored and processed across the OSS, BSS, mediation, SIEM, and tenants on the service assurance platform, due 2027-03-31 (POAM-009).
Group contingency planning policy applies (POL-03).
The OSS/BSS contingency plan covers failover to provider B, recovery order from the BIA, and coordination with the NOC for Part 4 notices.
BSS failover was tested in 2026-04. Gap: the service assurance platform has never been failed over with all three tenants (Carrier NOC, Engineering, Tower alarm center) (POAM-013).
Backups are kept in an immutable vault in provider B.
Provider B hosts warm disaster recovery copies of the BSS and OSS.
Daily immutable backups of OSS, BSS, and mediation databases; nightly network element configuration backups (acquired regions excepted; see P07 Carrier sample).
Restores of tier 1 data are tested each quarter.
Recovery and reconstitution follow the BIA order with integrity checks before reconnection.
Group identification and authentication standard applies (POL-02).

Workforce users authenticate through SYS-G1. Network element administrators authenticate through TACACS+ backed by SYS-G1 with MFA, except in the acquired regions, where access elements and 22 SBCs use shared local accounts (gap 1; POAM-010).
Phishing-resistant MFA for all privileged IT accounts.
MFA with number matching for all non-privileged workforce and outsourced agent accounts.
Network elements authenticate to the management plane with device certificates or SNMPv3 credentials.
Identifiers are unique, assigned by identity governance, and never reused.
Authenticators are managed in SYS-G1 and the PAM vault. Service account secrets for OSS integrations are covered by POAM-002.
Passwords are checked against breached-password lists and must be at least 14 characters for workforce accounts.

Customers authenticate to the portal, app, and chatbot with a password set without biographical or account information, plus optional app-based MFA. Gap: the chatbot account recovery pilot accepted account number and SSN4 (gap 4; disabled 2026-08-07; POAM-012); the acquired regions' legacy BSS does not send all change notices (POAM-029).
evidence: Portal configuration; chatbot release notes; P07 test

implementation_statement: Group incident response policy applies (POL-03).
Incident responders and NOC shift leads complete incident training each year.
Technical playbooks are tested each quarter. The cross-division notification exercise is tracked under IR-8.

24x7 incident handling by the group SOC with Carrier NOC and lawful-intercept liaisons. Gap: playbooks do not tell responders to check 911 and tower lighting effects before containment actions on shared platforms (POAM-005).
Incidents are tracked in one register that also serves as the CPNI breach record (64.2011(d)).

responsible_role: Carrier Senior Vice President, Regulatory and Compliance
implementation_statement: CPNI breaches are reported to the USSS and FBI through the FCC reporting facility within 7 business days of reasonable determination; outage notices follow Part 4. Matrix gaps are under IR-8.
Forensic and breach counsel support through the insurer panel; telecommunications counsel on retainer.

The group incident response plan exists. Gap: it does not yet cover FAA lighting reports, CALEA compromise reports, or Engineering customer notices, and the multi-regulator matrix has not been exercised (gap 8; POAM-004).
Vendor remote maintenance of OSS/BSS components goes through PAM with named accounts and recording; network equipment vendors connect through the jump hosts.
Cloud media sanitization is inherited from providers (SOC 2 reports); returned network element storage is wiped under the Carrier disposal procedure.
Authorized access lists for the 6 regional NOC data centers are reviewed quarterly.
Badge, PIN, and mantrap control at regional NOC data centers; lawful-intercept rooms have separate access.
Cameras and alarms at NOC data centers are monitored by the group security operations center.
Group planning policy applies; the Carrier supplement is aligned to 2026 group policy.
This SSP; reviewed at least annually and after major change.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) acknowledged by all workforce and outsourced agents, including CPNI rules.
Security architecture follows the group reference architecture: zero-trust access, management plane separation, and tenant isolation (tenant work in progress, AC-3).
Group information security program plan aligned to CSF 2.0.
The Group CISO leads the program and reports to the board risk committee quarterly.
Group risk management strategy with acceptance authorities by level (P01).
Group personnel security policy applies.
Background checks for employees and outsourced agents with CPNI access; lawful-intercept staff have enhanced checks.
Access is removed within 4 hours of termination for employees (outsourced agents covered by POAM-001).
Outsourced contact center contracts require screening, CPNI training, and leaver notice.
The disciplinary process expressly covers CPNI misuse (POL-01 4.7).

control_name: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information
implementation_statement: Carrier processing of CPNI is limited to the purposes in 47 U.S.C. 222(c)-(d) and approved marketing. Gap: affiliate access on the shared platform has no documented authority (POAM-009).
CPNI purposes are documented for BSS and marketing uses. Gap: purposes are not documented for affiliate operators and for SIEM copies of CPNI (POAM-009).

responsible_role: Carrier Senior Vice President, Regulatory and Compliance
implementation_statement: Opt-out and opt-in approvals are recorded in the BSS approval flag, checked before use, and kept at least 1 year.

responsible_role: Carrier Senior Vice President, Regulatory and Compliance
implementation_statement: CPNI notices meet 64.2008(c) and are sent every two years to opt-out customers (last mailing 2025-10).
Group risk assessment policy applies (POL-01 4.3).
FIPS 199 categorization in SSP section 6: High.
Carrier and group risk analyses (P01) cover the boundary each year.
Supply chain risk assessment for critical network and software suppliers (screening gap under SR-3).

Continuous scanning of IT assets. Gap: authenticated scanning does not yet cover network elements and SBCs in the acquired regions, and the 14-day target for known exploited vulnerabilities was met for 81% of network devices (gap 3; POAM-006).
Risk responses are tracked in P01 and P07 with owners and dates.
Criticality analysis identifies the service assurance platform, AAA, and the CDR store as critical components.
Contracts for components in the boundary include security, CPNI, and incident notice requirements.
Security engineering principles (least privilege, defense in depth, secure defaults) are applied in design reviews.
External services (cloud providers, CCaaS, chatbot vendor, bill print vendor) are reviewed before use and each year (vendor findings in the P07 Carrier sample).
Developer configuration management through the group code repository with protected branches.
Static and dynamic testing in the pipeline for portal, API gateway, and integration code.
Unsupported components are tracked; the 9 SBCs past vendor support are on the replacement plan under SI-2.
DDoS protection for the portal and API gateway from provider A; network DDoS scrubbing for customer traffic is separate.
Boundary protection through the provider A hub and regional NOC firewalls. Gap: SYS-E1 tunnels terminate inside the management plane in the acquired regions (gap 7; POAM-024).

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default, allow by exception at every hub and NOC firewall.
Data in transit is encrypted (TLS 1.2 or higher; IPsec between NOCs and the cloud).
Cryptographic protection for all transmissions crossing untrusted networks.
Customer-managed keys in the cloud key management service with rotation.
FIPS-validated cryptographic modules where available.
Data at rest is encrypted for all databases and object storage in the boundary.
Group system and information integrity policy applies.

Flaw remediation for IT components meets group targets. Gap: 9 of 140 SBCs run releases past vendor support and network device patching for known exploited vulnerabilities met the 14-day target 81% of the time (gap 3; POAM-011).
EDR on all servers and endpoints in the boundary.
24x7 SOC monitoring. Gap: management plane logs from the acquired regions, the SYS-E1 gateways, and the RMU platform are not in the SIEM (POAM-003).

control_name: Automated Tools and Mechanisms for Real-time Analysis
implementation_statement: Automated analysis through SIEM correlation and orchestration.
Inbound and outbound traffic at the hub and NOC edges is monitored for anomalies, including large CDR transfers.
The SOC receives CISA, FBI, and vendor advisories and assigns them to owners within 1 business day.
File integrity monitoring on OSS/BSS servers; network element images are verified against vendor hashes before installation.
Records retention: CPNI approval records 1 year (64.2007(a)(3)), campaign records 1 year (64.2009(c)), breach records 2 years (64.2011(d)), CDRs 24 months online.
Group supply chain risk management plan covers network equipment and software suppliers.

Supply chain controls exist for strategic suppliers. Gap: covered equipment screening (FCC Covered List; FAR 52.204-25) is a manual requisition check with no record, and the Carrier's 47 CFR 1.50007 certification relies on it (gap 10; POAM-007).
Network equipment is bought from authorized channels with contract terms on authenticity and support life.
Critical suppliers are reviewed each year (SOC reports or questionnaires).
